KV cache and prefix caching behavior
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sam Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:07] Martin Gomez: Martin here, CTO.
[00:00:09] Aisha Khan: Aisha, infra.
[00:00:11] Leo Tan: Leo, security.
[00:00:13] Priya Menon: Priya, ML.
[00:00:15] Jamal Reed: Jamal, DevOps.
[00:00:18] Karen Wu: Karen from Redwood, SE on the pilot.
[00:00:20] Sam Patel: Great. Agenda  204 quick status on networking, any blockers for peering, then routing/fallbacks, kernel/runtime upgrade schedule, benchmarks, then recap and action items.
[00:00:35] Martin Gomez: Sounds good. On networking, we tried the first peering step last night, we saw traffic but it looks like some outbound egress is being dropped by our firewall, some ports maybe.
[00:00:48] Aisha Khan: Yeah, we're seeing TCP resets to Redwood endpoints on 10.2.18. I think our security team changed a rule yesterday; we need the exact IP ranges to allow.
[00:00:56] Sam Patel: Understood. Karen, can you remind them of the exact CIDR ranges and ports we need?
[00:01:02] Karen Wu: Sure  2 for the control plane egress we need 52.14.32.0/22 and 34.76.0.0/16 (note: these are example public egress ranges), tcp 443 for control, and optionally tcp 853 if you're doing DNS over TLS to our resolvers. For the data plane we prefer peered private CIDR: we'll accept the peering CIDR you propose and we route internally over the VPC.
[00:01:28] Jamal Reed: Quick question  2 the peering, is it AWS VPC peering or are you recommending Transit Gateway? We currently use TGW for cross-account routing.
[00:01:36] Karen Wu: TGW is fine and often recommended for multi-account setups, we just need a route back to our subnets; the important part is you allow the peered CIDRs and accept our route propagation.
[00:01:45] Martin Gomez: Okay, we'll validate TGW config.
[00:01:48] Leo Tan: From security, once the peering is up we need to ensure audit logs show egress destination and we need KMS integration proof. Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for token keys?
[00:01:58] Karen Wu: Yes  2 Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and you can bring your own keys. For on-prem HSM we have an integration guide; we'll share the docs. There may be extra steps for key rotation we can walk through.
[00:02:10] Leo Tan: Perfect. Also need SOC2 artifacts.
[00:02:13] Sam Patel: We'll attach our SOC2 cert and the security pack after the call.
[00:02:17] Priya Menon: On the ML side, we ran the sample prompts and saw 120 150 ms token latency in the hosted path but once we moved to the private runtime latency bumped to ~260 ms for 2k tokens, there's a weird tail.
[00:02:31] Karen Wu: That's useful. Can you share the payload sizes and model config? Are you using kv-cache enabled models and are you hitting cold-starts?
[00:02:40] Priya Menon: We're using the 8k seq Llama-variant quantized to 4-bit (we thought it was stable)  2 KV cache is enabled. We saw a few larger-than-expected GC pauses on the host side, maybe the runtime kernel is doing a copy.
[00:02:52] Karen Wu: This aligns with a known kernel path we rolled last week; there's an upcoming runtime build with improved KV cache allocation and faster matmul kernels. We want to schedule an upgrade window  2 it should reduce that tail by 30 40% in many cases.
[00:03:05] Sam Patel: Target is to get that in pilot soon. Karen, what's the risk during the upgrade? Any rollback plan?
[00:03:11] Karen Wu: Risk is low; we'll run canary on a subset of nodes, real-time tracing, and automatic fallback to the previous runtime if we see regressions. For your pilot, we suggest scheduling a maintenance window (about 2 hours) so we can monitor.
[00:03:25] Aisha Khan: When you say fallback to previous runtime, is that a model-variant fallback or cluster-level? If we have live traffic, we need a routing policy to avoid user impact.
[00:03:33] Karen Wu: We can do routing at the route level  2 you can set a policy to route traffic to hosted Redwood endpoints or to a lower-tier dedicated pool while the upgrade runs. We can also implement header-based routing if you want to cutover by tenant.
[00:03:44] Martin Gomez: I want a guaranteed fallback to hosted for critical flows.
[00:03:47] Sam Patel: Noted  2 we'll add explicit routing policy configs for critical endpoints.
[00:03:50] Jamal Reed: Another practical thing  2 DNS resolution. Right now, some of our internal queries are attempting to resolve your internal hostnames and getting NX. Should we be using private hosted zones?
[00:03:59] Karen Wu: Private hosted zone is the cleanest; otherwise we publish reachable A records to your VPC. We'll include a DNS guide in the peering checklist.
[00:04:08] Priya Menon: Back to latency  2 is there a recommended quantization profile? We tried q4f16 and q4_0 and saw different behavior across kernels.
[00:04:16] Karen Wu: Our Optimize team typically recommends q4_CPU-friendly profile for inference on older kernels and a more aggressive q4_0 for the newer runtime; we'll document which kernel matches which quantization. For your tests, run both and report perplexity delta and token quality metrics.
[00:04:29] Priya Menon: Will do. We'll collect the eval prompts we used.
[00:04:33] Leo Tan: On audit logs  2 do you provide token-level logs or only aggregate? We need redaction capabilities before logs leave our VPC.
[00:04:40] Karen Wu: By default, detailed logs are available within the Private deployment and can be shipped to your SIEM; we support redaction rules and audit log sinks. We'll send the log schema.
[00:04:50] Sam Patel: Great. Quick check on routing timeouts  2 Jamal, you mentioned some 504s earlier?
[00:04:55] Jamal Reed: Yes, during peak retries we saw intermittent 504s when the KV cache misses spiked. It looked like a burst pattern from a nightly job.
[00:05:03] Karen Wu: For that pattern we can suggest request-level retries, longer connect timeout, and temporary burst capacity. Also prefix caching can reduce repeated KV misses if the workload is similar.
[00:05:13] Sam Patel: Actionable: Karen to draft tuning config (timeouts/retries/batching) and Priya to run a re-run with prefix caching enabled.
[00:05:20] Priya Menon: I'll schedule that.
[00:05:22] Martin Gomez: Any blockers on our side?
[00:05:24] Aisha Khan: We need the exact peering CIDRs, the DNS guide, and any outbound IPs for the control plane. Otherwise I'll open a ticket to change the firewall rules.
[00:05:33] Sam Patel: We'll send the network packet after this call.
[00:05:36] Karen Wu: On the runtime upgrade timeline  2 our dev team is targeting the build to be ready next week; we should aim for the maintenance window the week after. If you're okay, we'll shoot for March 2nd (we'll confirm).
[00:05:49] Martin Gomez: March 2nd is viable. We'll aim to have peering validated before then.
[00:05:54] Leo Tan: Please give us the org-level contract for KMS usage so security can pre-approve.
[00:05:58] Sam Patel: We'll include that in the security pack.
[00:06:00] Karen Wu: Also, Priya  2 a quick note on benchmarking: run both 512 and 8k sequence tests, with and without prefix caching, and include token distribution; that helps us tune batch sizes and kernel selection.
[00:06:12] Priya Menon: Noted. We'll run those and send results.
[00:06:15] Jamal Reed: One small friction  2 our ops team prefers a Terraform module for peering. Do you have a reference module we can adapt?
[00:06:22] Karen Wu: We have an infra repo with Terraform snippets and a small module for TGW/VPC peering. I'll share that link.
[00:06:28] Sam Patel: Okay, quick housekeeping  2 any regulatory or data residency concerns?
[00:06:33] Martin Gomez: Helix processes EU and US PII; we need data-at-rest encryption and audit trails kept in-region for EU workloads.
[00:06:41] Karen Wu: Redwood Private supports regional deployments and you can pin nodes to EU regions and enforce KMS with EU-resident keys. We'll include the region mapping doc.
[00:06:52] Leo Tan: Also need an SLA for latency percentiles for the pilot  2 what's the baseline you commit to for the Dedicated/private path?
[00:06:59] Sam Patel: For pilots we don't usually sign an SLA but we provide performance targets  94 for dedicated/private we aim for p50 < 150ms token for common small batches; we'll capture real numbers after the benchmark and discuss SLA as we move to reserved capacity.
[00:07:12] Martin Gomez: Fair.
[00:07:14] Priya Menon: Any notes about model version pinning and rollouts? We want stable model versions for production.
[00:07:19] Karen Wu: You can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We'll show that in the rollout doc.
[00:07:27] Sam Patel: Cool. Let's recap  204 action items and owners:
[00:07:31] Sam Patel: Redwood: send network diagram, peering CIDRs, DNS guide, Terraform snippets, security pack (SOC2 + KMS + audit log schema). Karen: peering checklist, runtime upgrade plan, tuning config.
[00:07:44] Martin Gomez: Helix: provide firewall snapshots, peering CIDR to use, and confirm maintenance window availability by 2026-02-20.
[00:07:53] Jamal Reed: We'll aim to validate TGW routes by Friday.
[00:07:56] Sam Patel: Next sync  94 same time next week. We'll expect benchmark artifacts from Priya and the peering confirmation from Aisha.
[00:08:03] Priya Menon: I'll upload the results to the shared drive and ping the group.
[00:08:07] Karen Wu: I'll attach the runtime changelog and the canary plan.
[00:08:10] Leo Tan: Thanks all.
[00:08:11] Martin Gomez: Thanks.
[00:08:13] Sam Patel: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[00:08:16] [call ends]
